purpose: Use the surviving-object GitHub layer to decide which British, and only narrowly relevant American, historical sources deserve future ingestion into the main nineteenth-century microscopy corpus. This replaces broad geographic expansion as the active research direction.

scope.core: United Kingdom microscopy, especially nineteenth-century slide preparation, circulation, commerce, teaching, comparison, and material publication.
scope.secondary: United States only where British sources already cite, review, exchange, purchase, or otherwise connect to the American object/text system.
scope.paused: Further global slide-bibliography expansion for geographic completeness.
scope.global_bibliography_state: slide-locked-pass-17; 197 verified entries; no pass-18 merge.
scope.frozen_object_survey_state: 307 discovery nodes / 155 strict nineteenth-century nodes; CLOSED_2026-08-09

working_model.historical_corpus: discursive/event layer: journals, catalogues, advertisements, correspondence, society proceedings, manuals and period texts
working_model.github_object_layer: surviving-object reverse index: labels, series numbers, cabinet positions, collection catalogues, accession systems, archival cards and present custody
working_model.ingestion_rule: Add a source to the historical corpus only when the surviving-object layer changes the historical question or closes a high-value object-text relation. Modern museum pages remain metadata/evidence pointers rather than nineteenth-century corpus text.

new_knowledge_from_crosswalk.result: Slides acquire successive addresses: glass geometry and finder coordinates, maker labels, series/catalogue numbers, cabinet positions, society inventories and later museum accessions. This makes retrieval and re-addressing a historical problem rather than a metadata nuisance.

Postal Microscopical Society circuits linked travelling slides to manuscript books, notes, drawings, damage liability, valuation, packing and postage. The circulating epistemic unit was larger than the slide alone.
Named Norman and Topping preparations were later used as reference/test objects for judging objectives. Commercial identity could stabilize an object enough for optical comparison after purchase.

Elcock now links field collection, washing/separation, mounting media, postal-society interpretation, standardized Foraminifera Type Slides, price, retailer network and surviving Whipple workshop material.

Cole's synchronized preparation-plus-text serial, Elcock's commercial comparative Type Slide, ordinary catalogue offerings, replicated published sets and anatomical serial sections must remain analytically distinct. Numbering or circulation alone does not make a slide a publication.

future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.target: Arthur C. Cole, Studies in Microscopical Science, vols. I-II
future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.why: Current corpus is rich in notices and reviews of Cole but comparatively weak in Cole's own preparation-by-preparation text. Full ingestion can recover issue order, preparation methods, mounting materials, slide/coverslip standards and the synchronized relation among preparation, plate and letterpress.
future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.special_question: Preserve source-level attribution differences between A. C. Cole and Martin J. Cole rather than harmonizing preparator responsibility.
future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.action_when_resumed: Unpack both volumes, structure by issue/preparation, deduplicate against UK master corpora, ingest only genuinely new passages/records.

future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.target: Microscopical News and Northern Microscopist, vol. IV (1884)
future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.why: The exact Charles Collins Jr. 'Fish Scales' notice is located at p. 109, but a full-volume pass is preferable because surrounding trade notices, mounting practice and local-society material may add more than the single known hit.
future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.action_when_resumed: Acquire/ingest the whole 1884 volume, not p.109 alone; deduplicate against existing Northern regional material.

future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.target: H. L. Smith, Diatomacearum Species Typicae, Century III notice/article
future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.why: The correct 1878 American Journal of Microscopy and Popular Science volume is located, while the UK corpus already preserves a detailed Century I bridge describing 100 slides, five pasteboard trays, numbered catalogue/labels, diamond-written numbers and exchanged material.
future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.action_when_resumed: Recover the Century III pages only; do not start a general US microscopy sweep.

future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.target: Frederic Kitton, Norfolk Diatoms Series III-IV
future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.why: Series I-II are already textually closed while surviving Farlow evidence shows the larger I-IV / nos. 1-100 system. III-IV prospectus/notices would complete the publication/distribution sequence efficiently.
future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.action_when_resumed: Search contemporary prospectuses, exchange columns and reviews for Series III-IV; preserve set number versus physical-copy count.

future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.target: John Thomas Norman 1872 catalogue + St Andrews labels
future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.why: The 2,584-offering catalogue, surviving Norman-labelled slides, secondary exchange and later use of Norman preparations as objective-test objects can produce a catalogue commodity → surviving object → epistemic reuse chain.
future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.action_when_resumed: Transcribe catalogue rows and St Andrews labels, then search the UK corpus by exact subject/maker wording.

future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.target: Andrew Pritchard 1837 preparation catalogue + Whipple cabinet
future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.why: Later UK reporting already preserves prices/categories for transparent, opaque, dozen and fossil-wood preparations; the Whipple cabinet retains Pritchard-labelled commercial mounts alongside homemade and broken slides.
future_corpus_ingestion_priorities.action_when_resumed: Locate the original 1837 catalogue, then compare advertised categories with surviving labels, case/tray architecture and later cabinet reuse.

object_metadata_only_targets.use: labels, raw packets, tools, mounting media, unfinished material and finished slides as reverse-index evidence; do not ingest museum prose into the historical corpus

object_metadata_only_targets.target: Oxford History of Science Museum / RMS cabinet and archive
object_metadata_only_targets.use: close already itemized journal receipt/exhibition events to old society indexes and surviving slide identifiers
search Cole and other already-known publication/product names in label/cabinet data before requesting new digitization
replicate/set-number evidence and item addresses; historical American text only where it intersects UK reception/exchange
cards, series/section positions and technical crosswalk as a narrow US comparator, not a new US corpus

object_metadata_only_targets.target: Bailey / Boston Society of Natural History
object_metadata_only_targets.use: follow the already-present 1857 British bequest notice only if accession/catalogue evidence for the collection survives

object_metadata_only_targets.target: Oscar W. Richards Collection, Smithsonian NMAH
object_metadata_only_targets.use: reverse bibliography for trade literature, advertisements and company history; do not ingest the retrospective archive wholesale

stop_rules: Do not continue global bibliography expansion for coverage alone.
Do not treat modern museum collection descriptions as nineteenth-century corpus text.
Do not start broad US microscopy harvesting; follow only UK-linked American actors/series.
Do not open new medium domains such as geological thin sections without a separate scope decision.
Do not spend substantial time on source acquisition until the project is actively resumed for reading/writing.
resume_trigger: When the microscopy project becomes an active reading/writing priority, begin with Cole rather than with further discovery.
